priority.rationale: Two exact official-paper/key matches; prerequisite value and a clear misconception. Eight-paper sample is not used to claim frequency or forecast marks.

pyqs.independentSolution: Write nA=1−x, nB=x, nHe=1. Kc=(x/10)/((1−x)/10)=x/(1−x)=4, so x=0.8 mol. RT/V=0.082×400/10=3.28 atm per mol. pHe=3.28, pB=2.624, pA=0.656; sum 6.56 atm and pB/pA=4. He absent from equilibrium expression but present in total pressure.

pyqs.answer: Kp = px²/(a²−x²), in the paper’s pressure convention
pyqs.independentSolution: Start with only a mol A in A⇌B+C; equilibrium amounts a−x,x,x and total a+x, not a. Partial pressures are p(a−x)/(a+x), px/(a+x), px/(a+x). Kp=pB pC/pA=px²/[(a+x)(a−x)]. Domain a>0,0<x<a. Dimensionless thermodynamic K uses p/p° instead of p; the article states the exam convention.

targetQuestionText: A 10 L flask initially contains 1 mol of helium and 1 mol of A, with no B. At 400 K, A(g) ⇌ B(g) has Kc = 4.0. Assuming ideal gases and R = 0.082 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, find the equilibrium partial pressures of helium and B.
difference: Gas stoichiometry, inert-gas accounting and partial pressures; does not reteach buffer pH or Nernst cell voltage.
